subChunks.title: JPA Entities & Mapping

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: JPA is the bridge between Java's object world and the relational database world. Annotate your class correctly and Hibernate handles the translation — CREATE TABLE, INSERT, SELECT — all generated.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Create a plain Java class Product with fields: Long id, String name, double price. Override toString() returning "Product[id=1, name=Wand, price=29.99]". Print an instance.
guidedPractice.hint: toString() returns "Product[id=" + id + ", name=" + name + ", price=" + price + "]".

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What JPA annotation generates the primary key automatically? What GenerationType options exist?

options: Delegates primary key generation to the database's auto-increment column
questions.answer: Delegates primary key generation to the database's auto-increment column
questions.explanation: IDENTITY uses the database's built-in auto-increment (e.g., PostgreSQL SERIAL / MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT).

subChunks.title: Spring Data Repositories

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Derived query methods feel like magic — you name the method and Spring writes the SQL. Under the hood it parses your method name at startup and generates a JPQL query. Use @Query for anything complex.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Demonstrate derived query naming: write method signatures (as strings) for: find by email, find all where active is true, find top 5 ordered by createdAt descending. Print each.
guidedPractice.hint: Print the method names as strings: findByEmail, findByActiveTrue, findTop5ByOrderByCreatedAtDesc.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: How does Spring Data JPA generate queries from method names? When should you use @Query instead?

questions.prompt: What does JpaRepository provide over CrudRepository?
options: Pagination and sorting support (findAll(Pageable), findAll(Sort)) and batch operations
questions.answer: Pagination and sorting support (findAll(Pageable), findAll(Sort)) and batch operations
questions.explanation: JpaRepository extends PagingAndSortingRepository which extends CrudRepository, adding pagination and sorting.

subChunks.title: Relationships, Fetching & N+1 Problem

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: The N+1 problem is the silent performance killer. You fetch 100 orders. Then your code accesses each order's lines — 100 more queries. One query to fetch them all with JOIN FETCH is the cure.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate the N+1 problem in pure Java: given a list of 3 order IDs, print the number of 'queries' needed if you fetch lines separately for each order (N+1), vs. one join query.
guidedPractice.hint: N+1 queries = 1 (for orders) + orderCount (for lines). JOIN FETCH = 1 query.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the N+1 query problem. How does JOIN FETCH solve it?

questions.prompt: What is the default fetch type for @OneToMany?
options: LAZY — related entities are loaded on demand
EAGER — related entities are always loaded
questions.answer: LAZY — related entities are loaded on demand
questions.explanation: @OneToMany defaults to LAZY. @ManyToOne defaults to EAGER. Prefer LAZY + JOIN FETCH for controlled loading.

subChunks.title: Projections, Transactions & Auditing

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Never load a full entity when you only need two fields — projections are the scalpel to the entity's sledgehammer. And always annotate service methods with @Transactional — it defines your unit of work.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Demonstrate transaction simulation: create a TransactionManager with beginTransaction(), commit(), and rollback(). Run a successful transaction and print Begin, Commit. Then a failed one: Begin, Rollback.
guidedPractice.hint: execute() calls beginTransaction(), then commit() if success==true, else rollback().

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What does @Transactional(readOnly = true) do and why should read operations use it?

questions.prompt: What is the benefit of using JPA interface projections?
options: Load only specific columns, reducing memory and query overhead
questions.answer: Load only specific columns, reducing memory and query overhead
questions.explanation: Projections tell JPA to SELECT only the needed columns. For list endpoints returning summaries, this is significantly more efficient.

questions.prompt: @Transactional(readOnly = true) can improve performance for read-only operations.
questions.explanation: readOnly=true hints to the JPA provider (e.g., Hibernate) and database driver to optimize for reads — no dirty checking, possible read replicas.
